notes.decision: Lycopolitan collective 'the four' (= Sah. ⲡϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ); cf. accumulated entry ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ. Used four times on this page in the cosmological enumeration of the Four Great Works.

The ordinal 'second' appears twice (lines 23 and 25), once introducing the kind and once recapitulating it. This is likely either dittographic elaboration ('the second kind is the eight earths... [namely] the second kind is from this earth...') or a scribal slip. I retain both as 'second kind' since the sequence first/second/third/fourth is otherwise complete (lines 20, 23, 27, 31).
Read as Lyc. variant of ⲱⲗ/ⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'be drawn together, be gathered.' With ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲣⲁⲩ 'into them' yields 'gathered into them.' Could alternatively be a relative form of ⲉⲗ (ⲱⲗ) 'roll/twist together.'

Anomalous form. Most likely a Lycopolitan compound ⲧⲁ-ⲡⲓⲱⲧ '(she-)of-the-Father' or simply a dialectal form of ⲡⲓⲱⲧ 'the Father' (with feminine relative ⲧⲁ-). Given the editor's restoration in line 34 of [ⲙⲛ ⲧⲁⲧⲙⲉⲩ ⲛ-] 'with the Mother of —,' the standard Manichaean Father/Mother of Life pair is in view. Translated 'the Father (of Life)' with this caveat.

Qualitative of ⲛⲁϣⲉ 'be many/great' with 3sg.f. subject ⲉⲥ-/ⲥ̄ — 'she is great/abundant.' The feminine pronoun refers to ⲧⲥⲫⲁⲓⲣⲁ (sphere) or to the lacunous noun ending in -ⲉ that 'she-is-great' modifies.

Translated 'her lash/affliction' tentatively. ⲉⲥⲓϣ likely = ⲉⲥⲏϣ 'blow, lash, stripe' with feminine possessive ⲡⲉⲥ-. The feminine antecedent is uncertain (perhaps Hyle or the kingdom of darkness from prior page). ⲁⲓ̈ⲧ following the gap reads as a qualitative ending (-ⲁⲓⲧ pattern: ⲇⲣⲁⲓⲧ, ⲧⲁⲭⲁⲓⲧ); the gap likely held the verbal stem.

Read as Lyc. ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise up' (per terminology guide; preserves vertical semantics). With ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ 'in shame' = 'raised up (exposed) in shame' — describing the punitive exhibition of the bound powers.

Translated 'principalities/leaders.' Lexeme of unclear etymology, possibly related to ⲝⲱⲣⲉ 'mighty' (= ϫⲱⲣⲉ) with prefix, or a Manichaean technical term for an archonic class. Recurs in lines 26-27 ('all the principalities of the kingship'), confirming a class of cosmic powers. Flagged for parallels.

Read as Lyc. perfect 'those whom they bound' from a verb ⲕⲁⲧϩ (possibly = ⲕⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'gather, bind' or ⲕⲱⲧϣ̄ 'turn, twist'). Context (in sequence with 'gathered them in,' 'fixed in the wheel,' 'bound them') confirms a binding/capturing sense.
Translated 'they reckoned them' from ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' (per accumulated vocab). The Lyc. form ⲟⲁⲡ shows vocalic doubling.

Translated 'in single accord' from ⲧⲱⲧ 'agreement, joining' (Lyc. ⲧⲟⲁⲧ). Could alternatively be 'in single grasp' if ⲧⲟⲁⲧ = ⲧⲱⲧ 'hand,' but the agreement-sense fits the cosmological binding image better.
ϣⲏϣ = 'be equal' (Sah. ϣⲏϣ); ⲛⲉⲙⲉⲩ = 'with them.' The clause indicates the Enmity-powers are equal/proportionate to their punishment-instrument.

Read as Lyc. variant of ⲛⲉⲩ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ 'they were there' (locative) — 'they were abiding there.' Alternative reading: ⲙⲏⲛ qualitative 'remaining.' Either yields 'they were (there) at the place where they stand fast in him.'

Translated 'upon the whole tree' reading ⲡϣⲉ as 'wood/tree' (ϣⲉ). Pairs with ⲡⲕⲁⲍ 'earth' as the dual destination of fallen matter cast back from the wheel. Could alternatively be 'the whole field' (ⲥⲱϣⲉ) or 'the whole abyss/depth' (ϣⲏ). Sense uncertain.

Translated 'they reigned to seize.' ⲁⲩⲣⲣⲟ = perfect 'they became kings/reigned'; ⲉϩⲉⲙⲁⲍⲧⲉ = ⲉ + ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'in order to grasp/seize.' The bound powers in the wheel are likened to those who once reigned by usurping kingship.

Translated 'multitude' (= ⲙⲏⲏϣⲉ) — interpreting the doubled-ⲟ as a Lyc. orthographic feature. Alternative 'midst' (ⲙⲏⲧⲉ) is also possible. The phrase 'in the multitude of mighty Aeons' fits the cosmological image of seizing kingship amid abundant powers.

Compound ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲝⲁⲓ- ('love' or 'boast') + ⲙ̄ⲗⲁⲍ ('strife,' per accumulated ⲙⲗⲟⲟϩ/ⲙ̄ⲗⲁϩ). Translated 'love-of-strife' = warlike contention. Listed alongside 'desire of women' and 'multitude of property' as constitutive vices of the bound archons.

Translated 'his hunger' reading ⲡⲉϩ- as Lyc. possessive 'his' (per accumulated vocab) + ϩⲕⲟ 'hunger.' Antecedent of 'his' is lost in the preceding lacunae but likely references one of the bound archonic powers whose hunger drove forth the animals.
Translated 'this king' (substantival ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ) rather than 'this kingship' — confirmed by line 6 ⲡⲓⲣⲡⲟ ⲉⲧϣⲏϣ ⲟⲩⲃⲉ ⲡϣⲓ ⲛⲧⲉϩⲙⲛⲧⲣⲡⲟ, where ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ (king) is contrasted with ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲟ (kingship).
Read as Lycopolitan ϥϣⲏϣ '(he) is equal,' parallel to ϣⲏϣ ⲟⲩⲃⲉ in line 3. The Lyc. ϩ for ϥ is regular before sibilants.

Rendered 'realms' rather than 'companions/associates' (the existing glossary entry) given the cosmological register: these are the bound powers in the sphere/Zone, the cosmic compartments where the archonic confederates are fixed. 'Realms' captures the spatialized reading; 'companions' would obscure the cosmographic function. Preserves the consistency that ⲇⲁⲙ designates dark-aligned cosmic entities.
Read ⲥⲁϣϩ as the numeral 'seven' (Lyc. ⲥⲁϣϥ̄/ⲥⲁϣϩ) — the seven planetary guides — paired with the immediately following ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ 'twelve' (zodiac signs). Standard Manichaean astronomical pair.

Translated 'they diminish' from a Lyc. reflex of ⲇⲟⲕⲡⲉ/ⲇⲱⲕⲡⲣ̄ 'be small, decreased' (Crum 511a). The antithetical pairing with ⲣ̄ⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'multiply' yields the cyclical fortune-image: wealth that the way-leaders cause both to grow and to diminish. Tentative — verb is rare.
